target: Route "bsi-counter" (round 16): best-response restart and bidirectional improvement — significance and novelty audit

findings.defect: NOT NEW. The statement "a Max vertex whose two options are a variable and a constant is switched at most twice along any improving run, by lem:switch" is already in frontier.tex, twice, in prose, with exactly the route's justification. The route presents it as new and as "stronger than the round-15 audit's version, which was stated only for R_BR" — but the document's own version is already stated for any improving run, i.e. at the route's generality. What the route actually adds is the ordering clause (all p->q switches precede all q->p), the Min-side dual bsc:minrev, and a numbered proof; that is housekeeping, not a result.
findings.evidence: /data/ssg-proof/frontier.tex l.4012-4014 (in the discussion after lem:max-tree): "a chain of $d$ Max vertices whose second actions are constants --- but such a chain fires at most twice, a Max vertex over a variable and a constant switching at most twice along any improving run (\Cref{lem:switch}), so it cannot be re-armed"; and l.5799 (rem:blowup-realise): "a vertex with one constant option flips at most twice (\Cref{lem:switch})". The round-16 briefing also records the round-15 rbr auditor's version. The route's LaTeX cites neither.

findings.defect: An UNPROVED quantitative claim sits inside the proposition environment: "So a $2^m-1$-round $R_{BR}$ run needs $k=\Omega(m)$ Min vertices but no more". Both halves fail. (i) $k\ge\log_2 p$ is a lower bound on $k$ only from a LOWER bound on the piercing number $p$; the route's own text says $p\le 9,\le 14,\le 22$ at $m=5,6,7$ came from a randomised greedy cover, i.e. they are UPPER bounds, from which no $\Omega(m)$ follows. The results block compounds this by reading "$p$ grows like about $1.55^m$" off a mixture of three exact values and three upper bounds. (ii) "but no more" is not established at all: a small piercing number is a necessary condition on a hypothetical run, and realisability by an actual stopping SSG is the entire difficulty (prop:auso-size, and the route's own failed searches). Only the negative direction — few guides can suffice combinatorially, so the guide count is not an obstruction — is supported, and only for the reflected-Gray run and the exhaustive $m\le3$ case.
findings.evidence: Route LaTeX, \begin{proposition}\label{bsc:pierce}, final sentence, versus the same block's own parenthesis "the first three exact by exhaustive search and the last three by a randomised greedy cover".

findings.defect: UNDERSOLD AND WEAKER THAN THE ROUTE'S OWN LEMMAS. bsc:const-cor plus thm:eval-stopfree plus lem:local-global already give a POLYNOMIAL ALGORITHM, not a bound for one rule: if every Max vertex has a successor from which no Max vertex is reachable (so val_sigma there is sigma-independent, lem:successor-closed), then Hoffman-Karp — indeed every switching rule — reaches an optimal sigma in at most 2m rounds, each round one evaluation of val_sigma; dually, by lem:duality applied to G-bar, if every Min vertex has a successor from which no Min vertex is reachable then Min's policy iteration halts in at most 2k rounds, each round one evaluation of val^tau. That is a bound of 2k INDEPENDENT of m and of R_BR, against the route's m(k+1) for R_BR only; and it is a candidate NINTH polynomial class, with |Vavg|, N and the other player wholly unrestricted. Concretely, on the paper's own Z_D (prop:escape-family) every Max vertex has the constant successor t_0 and the single Min vertex has t_1, so the corollary improves thm:bounded-components from 2^{Theta(N)} to O(N) on an instance the document already carries and already certifies as outside thm:few-avg, thm:few-escape, thm:kacyclic, thm:bounded-components and thm:few-denominator. The route states none of this; it frames the whole thing as "a new polynomial class for the rule" and stops.
findings.evidence: Route LaTeX \Cref{bsc:const-cor} and \Cref{bsc:clamp}; /data/ssg-proof/frontier.tex prop:escape-family (l.1763-1770): $M_j\to(s_{j-1},t_0)$, $W\to(s_D,t_1)$; thm:eval-stopfree (l.638), lem:successor-closed (l.2143), lem:duality, thm:bounded-components (l.4178).

findings.defect: The class is claimed but no member outside the existing eight is exhibited, which is the document's own standard (rem:kacyclic's warning, and the round-13 defect it records). Z_D is a member of both clamped classes but has min(m,k)=1, hence is trivially in P by the enumeration argument at thm:bsi-tracks, and it lies inside thm:escape-class. Every instance the route built is either one-player (L_n, H_m, CC, WD, SD: k=0) or acyclic (RD(n)), so none of them is outside thm:one-player / thm:kacyclic either. Until a clamped stopping instance is exhibited with min(m,k)=Theta(N), a=Theta(N), exponential common denominator, all three colours on one strongly connected component, escape exponent Theta(N), and no polynomial escape certificate — checked on the subgame reachable from v0 — the class claim is unverified.
findings.evidence: Route results block, bsc:clamp: "the clamped class has ceiling m(k+1)=O(N^2)" and the coverage list; no instance in out/ has k>1 except the random samples, and those are unstructured.

findings.defect: The proof is the proof of thm:bsi-tracks re-run. The potential Phi(sigma,U) counting U-greedy Max vertices, the fact that a switched vertex becomes U-greedy and unswitched vertices keep their status, and the "a block with one guide has at most m rounds" step are all verbatim in the existing proof; the route adds one telescoping line, the term sum_t d_t, and recovers m+(m+1)B exactly by d_t<=m. The route's LaTeX does say "refines", which is honest, but the results block promotes it to one of three headline contributions. For R_BR itself the bound R<=m(1+#guide changes) is vacuous whenever the guide changes every round, which is the generic case for a rule that recomputes a best response each round; it has content only on the clamped class, where the stronger 2k bound above applies anyway.
findings.evidence: /data/ssg-proof/frontier.tex, proof of thm:bsi-tracks (l.8368-8382): "Call $v\in\Vmax$ U-greedy at $\sigma$ ... and let $\Phi(\sigma,U)\in[0,m]$ count them ... a maximal block of consecutive rounds with $C_{\min}=\emptyset$ has at most $m$ rounds".

findings.defect: Part (a) — sigma' is a best response to tau iff it is val^tau-greedy — is the Bellman/Howard greedy-optimality theorem for the MDP obtained by freezing Min, i.e. lem:local-global relativised to a frozen guide, and it is already the working notion inside the proofs of thm:bsi-tracks and prop:bsi-oneplayer, which both speak of U-greedy and greedy vertices. Presented here as a new lemma with no attribution to standard dynamic programming and no cross-reference to lem:local-global. The reformulation of R_BR as sigma -> sigma[S_sigma cap Dis(sigma, sigma**)] IS a real clarification and is worth two sentences, but it is a repackaging, not a theorem. (From memory, unchecked: describing symmetric strategy improvement through the opponent's best response is also how van Dijk-Loho-Maat present their rule, whom rem:bsi-br already credits.)
findings.evidence: /data/ssg-proof/frontier.tex lem:local-global (l.3241), proof of prop:bsi-oneplayer (l.8168-8180, "Call $v\in\Vmax$ greedy if ..."), proof of thm:bsi-tracks (l.8368).

findings.defect: Inflated. Of the seven families listed as newly covered, L_n, H_m, CC(L,m), WD(e,j,m), SD(K) and "every one-player game" all have k=0, where bsc:clamp degenerates to R<=m — which is prop:bsi-oneplayer's argument, already in the document, and which the route itself concedes in bsc:clamp-rem. So the corollary's genuinely new coverage is: two-player clamped games, none of which the route exhibits with k>1.

SOUND, INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED, AND THE ONE ITEM WORTH INTEGRATING AS STATED. I rebuilt the 34-vertex realisation from out/witnesses.json and recomputed everything in exact rational arithmetic with my own core: greatest trap on the non-sinks is empty (stopping), w*=(13/64,1/4,1/32) by brute force over all profiles, R_BR = 3 from (0,0) in both the veto and the strict variant and for every best response, all-switches = 2,0,2,1 from the four starts, and def:bsi = 4 from ((0,0),0) in both variants with switch sets ({v_0},{}),({},{u}),({v_1},{}),({v_0},{}). Two things in it are genuinely new to the document: (i) 3 > h*(2)=2, the first instance anywhere in the paper where R_BR exceeds the all-switches AUSO ceiling at the same m — on G# R_BR takes 5 < 7 = h*(4) and on RD(n) it takes n < h*(n) — so cor:ceiling-general does not bound R_BR; (ii) a BSI run of 4 > |C| = 3, which upgrades prop:bsi-twice's "cannot be improved to a bound of |C| rounds BY SUCH MEANS" to an actual counterexample and corrects rem:readout's "Neither family exceeds |C| rounds".

findings.defect: GAP 2 is rem:readout(ii)'s obstruction transposed to the Min side, and the route does not advance it by a single instance. rem:readout already says the leapfrog makes reversals cheap but "each reversal consumes a fresh driver that switches once ... the obstruction is not the leapfrog but the recycling of its drivers"; bsc:reorder plus pigeonhole reproduces exactly that on the Min side. Worse, every instance the route built is clamped, and its own bsc:minrev then forbids more than one reversal per Min vertex — the measured chi is [1] on W_2 and M_3 and [1,...,1,0] on RD(n). verdict:
IS IT NEW? Partly, and the route's own ranking of what is new is wrong. bsc:const is a rediscovery of an observation frontier.tex already makes twice in prose with the same one-line proof (l.4013, l.5799); bsc:double-br is the Bellman greedy-optimality theorem, already the working notion inside the proofs of thm:bsi-tracks and prop:bsi-oneplayer, unattributed; bsc:reorder is the proof of thm:bsi-tracks with one telescoping line added, which the route's LaTeX does label honestly. Genuinely new: bsc:minrev (the Min dual, one line), bsc:clamp, and bsc:w2.

CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No oracle is assumed and nothing is target-equivalent. No barrier is claimed. bsc:clamp is a real polynomial bound and is not vacuous, but as a POLYNOMIAL CLASS it is unverified: no member outside the eight is exhibited, and every instance the route built is one-player (k=0) or acyclic. bsc:pierce's proposition contains an unproved sentence, and the numbers behind it are upper bounds used to support a lower-bound conclusion. Neither W_2 nor M_3 is a family — they are single instances, correctly presented as such, dyadic, built and verified from the game; I re-verified both from the raw successor lists in exact arithmetic and they hold exactly as stated.

VERIFICATION HONEST? Yes. The exact arithmetic is real, the realisations are built and checked from the games, the random sampling is labelled as non-evidence, and the failed searches are reported as failures. The one place the evidence does not support the claim is bsc:pierce's asymptotics.

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, stated more precisely than the route states it. The route's GAP 2 is a necessary condition and is already the document's known obstruction on the other side. The true gap is: EXHIBIT A build(n), STOPPING, WITH MEASURED GROWTH AT AT LEAST FIVE SIZES, ON poly(n) VERTICES, CARRYING A MIN VERTEX BOTH OF WHOSE OPTIONS ARE NON-CONSTANT AND WHOSE BEST-RESPONSE ACTION REVERSES OMEGA(n^c) TIMES ALONG THE R_BR RUN WITH EACH REVERSAL FLIPPING AT LEAST ONE MAX PREFERENCE (d_t >= 1 in bsc:reorder) — and the route has not produced a single instance in which any Min vertex reverses even twice, because every instance it built is clamped and its own bsc:minrev forbids it. What the route has actually established is the negative half: the clamped class, which is the only class in which it constructed anything, is capped at O(N^2) rounds and provably cannot carry the family. That is a genuine restriction on (DOWN) and should be recorded as such; it is not progress towards a family.

WOULD INTEGRATING IT MAKE THE PAPER BETTER OR WORSE? As delivered, WORSE. It would add a lemma the document already states twice, a theorem that is an existing proof re-run, a proposition whose stated conclusion is unproved, and an instance (M_3) that separates nothing — roughly four pages for one page of content, in a document whose value now depends on not restating itself.

Trimmed, BETTER, and the trimmed version contains one item worth more than the route claims for it. Integrate:
(1) bsc:w2, as a proposition with its 34-vertex realisation. It is verified, it gives h_BR(2) = 3 = 2^m - 1 against h*(2) = 2 — the first instance in the document where R_BR exceeds the all-switches AUSO ceiling, so cor:ceiling-general does not bound R_BR — and a BSI run of 4 > |C| = 3, which upgrades prop:bsi-twice from "not by such means" to a counterexample and corrects rem:readout's "Neither family exceeds |C| rounds". About one page. Its mechanism paragraph (bsc:w2-rem, the clamp that has not yet engaged inflating the guide) is worth keeping.
(2) A single numbered lemma carrying bsc:const, its ordering clause and its Min dual bsc:minrev, placed so that the prose at l.4013 and l.5799 CITES it instead of re-deriving it, and explicitly labelled as the formalisation of an observation the document already makes — plus, and this is the item with the highest value in the whole route, the corollary the route did not draw: on a stopping SSG in which every Max vertex has a successor from which no Max vertex is reachable, EVERY switching rule halts within 2|Vmax| rounds, so Hoffman-Karp with thm:eval-stopfree decides the game in 2m polynomial-time evaluations; dually, via lem:duality on G-bar, 2|Vmin| evaluations when every Min vertex has such a successor. That is a polynomial algorithm with a, N and the other player unrestricted; on the paper's own Z_D it replaces thm:bounded-components' 2^{Theta(N)} by O(N). Record it with the honest caveat that Z_D is a member but has min(m,k) = 1 and lies in thm:escape-class, and set as the open item: a clamped member with min(m,k) = Theta(N), a = Theta(N), exponential common denominator, all three colours on one SCC, escape exponent Theta(N) and no polynomial escape certificate, checked on the subgame reachable from v0 — with that, it is a ninth polynomial class; without it, it is a bound.
(3) bsc:reorder as one displayed inequality in a remark after thm:bsi-tracks, five lines, labelled a refinement.

Do NOT integrate: bsc:double-br as a lemma (two sentences in rem:bsi-br, cross-referenced to lem:local-global and attributed to Bellman/Howard greedy-optimality, from memory and unchecked); bsc:clamp in its m(k+1) form (superseded by the 2k bound in (2), and its coverage list is inflated); bsc:pierce (the conclusion inside the proposition is unproved; at most one sentence, restricted to m <= 4 where p is exact, saying that the guide count is not the obstruction); M_3 (a file reference at most); the search calibration (one sentence, already the document's standing practice).
